working_theory_before: The Experiment 13 normalization safety failure may be primarily caused by a pooled conformal threshold redistributing coverage asymmetrically between stress and non-stress classes.
working_theory_after: Class conditioning explains and substantially removes the class imbalance, but it does not restore the required safety level. The residual failure is therefore not merely a pooled-threshold artifact. Subject-level distribution shift or reliability remains the leading unresolved mechanism.

claim_updates.claim: A pooled conformal threshold caused the normalized representation's class-coverage imbalance.
claim_updates.reason: Class conditioning reduced the absolute class gap from 0.0972 to 0.0114.

claim_updates.claim: Class-Mondrian calibration is sufficient to repair normalized external coverage.
claim_updates.reason: Mean coverage reached only 0.8769 and stress coverage only 0.8712, both below the frozen 0.88 requirements.
Worst-subject coverage fell from 0.7083 to 0.6875, and the paired-subject coverage interval included zero.

claim_updates.claim: Balancing class coverage necessarily improves overall informativeness.
claim_updates.reason: Full-set frequency increased by 0.0240 versus normalized marginal calibration even though the class gap narrowed.

meno_j_implication: The engine converted an observed class asymmetry into a precise intervention, then rejected it as a complete J-jump. A mechanistic clue can be real without being sufficient for repair.
next_falsification_target: Freeze a subject-level reliability-gate study using only unlabeled onboarding diagnostics—such as train-to-subject shift, within-subject dispersion, sensor stability, and protocol version—and test whether it can select raw versus normalized representation without test-label access while preserving coverage.
